$comment: The ~kind discriminators. A value here is PERMANENT from the first identifier that uses it: there is no deprecation path, because deprecating a kind would break every citation carrying it. Derived on 2026-08-31 by auditing every shape-D collision across 4,093,000 documents and separating genuine parallel series from version copies, duplicate documents and unnumbered bulletins. Only two families survived that test.

rules.primary_series_takes_the_bare_leaf: Where a container holds parallel series, the PRIMARY series (the one the corpus is named for) carries no ~kind and the others do. This follows the AKN4Africa rule of never renumbering the original: adding a secondary series later must not change identifiers already minted for the primary one.
rules.permanent: Once any identifier uses a kind, that spelling is fixed forever. Enumerate a corpus's kinds BEFORE minting it.
rules.never_infer_from_level_classifier: Puerto Rico stores level_classifier='article' for BOTH its articles and its sections. The discriminator must come from the citation, not from a structural label.
rules.kind_comes_from_the_citation: A kind is assigned by matching `citation_pattern` against the document's own publisher citation, anchored at the end because the discriminator precedes the leaf. It is NEVER inferred from level_classifier, which Puerto Rico sets to 'article' for both its articles and its sections.
rules.kind_is_applied_uniformly_not_only_on_co: Where a citation matches, the kind is applied to EVERY such document, whether or not a sibling currently collides with it. Applying it only on collision would make an identifier depend on whether a sibling happens to exist, so adding one later would silently change an identifier already published.

kinds.description: A form or sample document issued alongside a rule, sharing its number.

evidence.container: Alabama Rules for Using Videotape Equipment to Record Court Proceedings

documents.title: Rule 3. The official record of court proceedings
Form 3. Sample Tags or Labels for Marking Exhibits

kinds.description: A numbered section of an act that also numbers its articles, where the two sequences overlap. Puerto Rico's leyes carry both an Articulo sequence and a Seccion sequence.

documents.title: Articulo 10. Legitimacion para presentar acciones judiciales
Seccion 10. Se elimina el Capitulo 6 de la Ley 21-2016

rejected.why_not_a_kind: These are separate RULE SETS, which is a container level, not a parallel series inside one container. Minnesota stores 14 of them under chapter 'pr' with byte-identical citation 'Minn. R. Prof. 4'. Modelling them as kinds would encode a corpus defect into a permanent identifier.
rejected.resolution: Fixed in the MN ingester and CUT OVER on 2026-09-02: the citable unit is the (code, subtype) pair, and the set's name is scraped from the publisher's own <h2 class="subtype_header"> rather than tabulated or invented. Eleven codes were found to hold 33 sets, so this was never a 'pr' problem. mn/court-rules now mints 958 documents with zero collisions. Note the primary-series rule above is load-bearing here: ap/rcap carries NO sub-heading because it is the shelf's own series, and reading that absence as a parse failure would have dropped 42 live appellate rules.

rejected.jurisdiction: wi, tn, al and other agency-guidance corpora
rejected.why_not_a_kind: These are document TITLES, surfacing because unnumbered bulletins derive their leaf from an issue date and two bulletins share a day. That is collision class B, and the remedy is spec rule B1 (slug from the title), not an unbounded kind vocabulary drawn from subject matter.
Version markers the audit's version regex did not catch. Collision class A: the same Work at different Expressions, which a Work identifier is correct to merge.
Part E and Part F of a policy manual. A container level, recovered correctly since the 2026-08-31 container-path fix.
